name: Großglockner Hochalpenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road is Austria's most iconic scenic highway: 48 km of alpine wonder, Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe, and the Pasterze Glacier.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous and heritage-protected Grossglockner High Alpine Road ranks among the boldest, most renowned, and most thrilling scenic highways in the entire alpine world. Spanning 48 kilometers with 36 masterfully engineered hairpin curves, this 1930s engineering marvel ascends to 2,504 meters at the Hochtor pass, seamlessly connecting Salzburg with East Tyrol and Carinthia. Embedded in the majestic high-alpine landscape of the Hohe Tauern National Park, the route reveals breathtaking vistas of sheer rock walls, blooming alpine meadows, and pristine glacier fields. The undisputed crown jewel along the road is the panoramic branch up to Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe at 2,369 meters, commanding an awe-inspiring view of Austria's highest peak, the 3,798-meter Grossglockner, and the vast Pasterze Glacier.

Route & Requirements

Driving the Grossglockner High Alpine Road requires no mountaineering fitness, though drivers, motorcyclists, and cyclists must maintain focus and sound brakes on sustained gradients of up to twelve percent. The route is peppered with turnouts, panoramic terraces, and thematic nature displays. At Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe, fully accessible footpaths connect to a contemporary visitor centre with multiple floors of exhibitions, a craft workshop, and a widescreen cinema. From here, the Gamsgrubenweg path leads through secure rock tunnels to vantage points overlooking the receding glacier and cascading waterfalls (approx. 1 hour walking, easy). Sturdy footwear and warm clothing are strongly advised even in midsummer, as sudden snowfall and icy gusts can occur at elevations exceeding two thousand meters.

Visit & Arrival

The road is open daily from early May to early November, depending on snow conditions (closed throughout winter). Northern access begins at Bruck and Fusch in Salzburg, while southern access approaches via Heiligenblut or from Lienz via the B107. The toll highway costs approx. €43.00 per car. In summer, the Glocknerbus connects Lienz and Zell am See directly with Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe on a regular schedule.

Tips

Watch friendly alpine marmots scampering across the rocks at Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe and scan the cliffs through spotting scopes for alpine ibex. A stop at the Wilhelm Swarovski Observatory with its high-power optical telescopes will delight wildlife enthusiasts.
preis: Toll road (day pass for passenger cars approx. €43.00)
